# KL2005 `host-path-volume`

A volume mounts a directory or file of the node.

Category: `security`. Severity: `warning`. Enabled by default.

## What it does

Reports every `hostPath` volume in a Pod and in the pod template of every workload
kind, except a container runtime socket, which KL2007 `docker-socket-mount` reports.

## Why it matters

A `hostPath` volume mounts a directory or file of the node into the container. The
container can then read whatever the node keeps there (credentials, logs, the files of
other pods) and, unless the mount is read only, change it. Mounting `/`, `/etc`,
`/var/lib/kubelet` or a container runtime socket hands over the node. The `baseline`
Pod Security Standard forbids `hostPath` volumes.

The data also stays on one node: when the pod moves, it finds a different directory,
or none. Some node agents need a `hostPath` (a log collector reading `/var/log`, a CSI
driver). For those, mount it read only where possible, then silence the finding for
that object and say why.

## Example

```yaml
volumes:
- name: data
  hostPath:
    path: /srv/app-data
    type: Directory
```

Use instead:

```yaml
volumes:
- name: data
  persistentVolumeClaim:
    claimName: app-data
```

Use a `configMap` or `secret` volume for configuration files, and `emptyDir` for
scratch space.
